paragraphs.en: Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living. The phrase “less is more” was actually first popularized by a German, the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who like other people associated with the Bauhaus, a school of design, emigrated to the United States before World War II and took up posts at American architecture schools. These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture, but none more so than Mies.

paragraphs.en: Mies's signature phrase means that less decoration, properly organized, has more impact than a lot. Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance. Like other modern architects, he employed metal, glass and laminated wood – materials that we take for granted today but that in the 1940s symbolized the future. Mies's sophisticated presentation masked the fact that the spaces he designed were small and efficient, rather than big and often empty.

paragraphs.en: The apartments in the elegant towers Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive, for example, were smaller – two-bedroom units under 1,000 square feet – than those in their older neighbors along the city's Gold Coast. paragraphs.en: The “Case Study Houses” commissioned from talented modern architects by California Arts & Architecture magazine between 1945 and 1962 were yet another homegrown influence on the “less is more” trend. Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing. In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life – few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers – but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.

案例（Case Study Houses项目名称的一部分）
研究（项目名称的一部分）
艺术（杂志名称的一部分）
和；并且（连接并列或承接的内容）
还；又（yet another整体为又一个）
定冠词，限定所说对象；通常不单译
更少的东西；更少的资源
是；处于（联系主语与状态）

phrases.meaning: 少即是多；以简约实现更好效果

auditV2.note: 杂志是委托者，建筑师受委托；1945至1962为项目年代。

sentences.en: Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing.

chunks.en: Aesthetic effect came
chunks.zh: 审美效果产生

chunks.en: from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing.
chunks.zh: 于周围景观、新材料和直截了当的细节处理

sentences.reorder: 无需调整语序，forthright 指不加掩饰的设计表达。
sentences.translation: 审美效果来自周围景观、新材料和直截了当的细节处理。

words.meaning: 定冠词，限定所说对象；通常不单译
和；并且（连接并列或承接的内容）
直截了当的；不加掩饰的

auditV2.note: 审美效果来自景观材料及直接细节处理，不是表面装饰堆砌。

sentences.en: In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life – few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers – but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.

chunks.en: In his Case Study House,
chunks.zh: 在他的案例研究住宅中

chunks.en: Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted
chunks.zh: 拉尔夫·拉普森可能预测错了

chunks.en: just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life
chunks.zh: 机械革命究竟会怎样影响日常生活

chunks.en: – few American families acquired helicopters,
chunks.zh: 很少有美国家庭购置了直升机

chunks.en: though most eventually got clothes dryers
chunks.zh: 尽管大多数家庭最终都买了干衣机

chunks.en: – but his belief
chunks.zh: 但他抱有的信念

chunks.en: that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable
chunks.zh: 即自给自足既可取又不可避免

chunks.en: was widely shared.
chunks.zh: 得到了广泛认同

sentences.reorder: 把长插入例子作为括注；that 信念内容放在“信念”前，was shared 为主句谓语。
sentences.translation: 拉尔夫·拉普森在他的案例研究住宅中，可能错误预测了机械革命会怎样影响日常生活——很少有美国家庭购置直升机，尽管大多数家庭最终都买了干衣机——但他认为自给自足既可取又不可避免，这一信念得到了广泛认同。
